content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am currently using [product_name] [version_no]. It seems to have installed correctly on my Mac M1 along with [product_name] [version_no]. However, when I try to run [product_name], nothing happens. [product_name] works as expected (both were installed together). I have installed both Corretto 8 and 11, but [product_name] still does not launch, even though installation appeared normal. Does anyone have any suggestions?
[product_name] [version_no] is not compatible with Mac OS [version_no] or Java Corretto. I therefore suggest using [version_no] as mentioned in the original post: [url]

A few years ago, I upgraded [product_name] from [version_no] to [version_no] on macOS 11. After the upgrade, my macOS was updated to version 12 and then 13, and [product_name] [version_no] still worked fine. For certain reasons, I had to repeat the upgrade from [version_no] to [version_no] on macOS 13, but it no longer worked. Additionally, in September 2023, the upgrade to [version_no] was no longer available on [company_name]'s website, though I still had a copy downloaded earlier. I did not investigate further, but I suspect that the upgrade package from the website encountered the same issue as the [version_no] package, likely related to execution attributes and macOS security policies. In early 2024, I purchased the DVD for [product_name] [version_no] (since [version_no] was unavailable). [version_no] installed successfully from the DVD, and I tested on both macOS 13 and 14. This has been my experience regarding [product_name] [version_no] compatibility with macOS.

analysis.insight_summary: Users have encountered issues running [product_name] [version_no] on Mac devices with newer hardware and recent versions of macOS. While installation appears successful, the application does not launch, in contrast to other [company_name] software that functions properly on the same system. User feedback highlights incompatibility with the newest macOS and Java environments, with a recommendation to use [version_no] for better support. Historically, [version_no] worked up to macOS versions 13-14 but cannot be installed or run reliably on the latest operating systems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] [version_no] to install and run successfully on their current Mac device and operating system, consistent with their previous experience using earlier versions and other [company_name] products.
